title: ASUS AI Tech 2026 Seoul South Korea
gist: Sponsored event recap (ASUS paid travel) from ASUS AI Tech 2026 in Seoul showing NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and Vera Rubin NVL72 systems. The key signal is the generational shift to all-liquid cooling: flipped GPU orientation lets eight Rubin GPUs fit in 1U versus 6U+ for air-cooled HGX, and fans are moving out of the chassis entirely, making rack density and power efficiency the binding constraint on data-center performance.

themes.theme: Rubin NVL8 density leap via liquid cooling

insights.claim: NVIDIA's HGX Rubin NVL8 generation flips GPU orientation on the baseboard to enable more efficient liquid cooling, a major design break from Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell-era HGX designs.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals a hardware architecture discontinuity that favors liquid-cooling supply chains over legacy air-cooled designs.
insights.quote: This generation flips the GPU orientation on the baseboard to enable more efficient liquid cooling.

insights.claim: Liquid-cooled HGX Rubin NVL8 lets eight GPUs fit in 1U instead of the 6U or more needed to air-cool an HGX baseboard.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Roughly 6x vertical density gain per 8-GPU node concentrates power per rack, raising demands on facility power and cooling infrastructure.
insights.quote: This design also lets the eight GPUs fit in 1U instead of taking 6U or more to air-cool the HGX baseboard

insights.claim: ASUS pairs the 1U liquid-cooled GPU segment with a separate chassis segment for CPUs, SSDs and DPUs, and offers hybrid or all-liquid cooling so nodes can fit data centers with differing cooling capabilities.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Hybrid-cooling options broaden addressable market to facilities not yet retrofitted for full liquid cooling, a practical adoption bridge.
insights.quote: The ability to use either hybrid cooling or all-liquid cooling in these nodes helps them fit into data centers with different capabilities.

insights.claim: Although individual Rubin GPUs may draw more power than Hopper-generation GPUs, the NVL8 domain holds more compute and memory, keeping more communication inside the node rather than going out to the scale-out fabric.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Larger in-node domains reduce reliance on scale-out networking per unit of work, shifting value toward NVLink and on-node memory.
insights.quote: more communication can stay within the node instead of having to go out to the scale-out fabric

insights.claim: The Rubin NVL8 platform brings a new generation of onboard NVLink Switch alongside high-speed NVIDIA scale-out networking to enable larger clusters.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA continues bundling interconnect and networking with GPUs, deepening platform lock-in beyond the accelerator itself.
insights.quote: NVIDIA also brings a new generation of NVLink Switch onboard

themes.theme: Rack-scale NVL72 and fanless liquid racks

insights.claim: ASUS markets its NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 and Vera Rubin NVL72 rack solutions as the 'ASUS AI Pod', built on liquid-cooled ORv3 trays.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: ASUS is positioning as a rack-scale NVIDIA integrator, competing for the same NVL72 build-outs as larger ODMs/OEMs.
insights.quote: ASUS also brought trays from its NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 and Vera Rubin NVL72 solutions that it calls the ASUS AI Pod.

insights.claim: The Vera Rubin NVL72 design shows a generational shift toward removing fans from the chassis and liquid-cooling everything in the rack to raise compute density and performance within a fixed power footprint.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Fully liquid-cooled racks expand the market for cold plates, CDUs and facility liquid loops while shrinking the role of server fans.
insights.quote: the generational shift toward moving fans out of the chassis and liquid-cooling everything in the rack

insights.claim: All-liquid-cooled design raises efficiency, which the author and event speakers framed as ultimately determining how much performance a data center can deliver.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Power-constrained data centers make cooling efficiency a direct lever on revenue-generating compute, not just an operating cost.
insights.quote: The all-liquid-cooled design increases efficiency, which ultimately determines how much performance you can get from a data center.

insights.claim: The ServeTheHome coverage of ASUS AI Tech 2026 in Seoul was sponsored, with ASUS paying the author's travel and the author moderating a panel at the event.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Vendor-sponsored framing warrants discounting promotional claims about ASUS products relative to independent benchmarks.
insights.quote: Of course, ASUS paid for my travel, so we have to say this is sponsored.
